annotations.title: Terrain of a ski or snowshoe tour

description: The terrain of one ski or snowshoe tour in the Alps, by the id from winter_tours: how steep it is and for how long, the aspects of the steep slopes, how much lies in avalanche terrain (ATES and ATM), stretch by stretch, and the grade explained with the words of the SAC scale and who gave it. Terrain only, computed from terrain models; not snow or avalanche conditions. Name ATES and ATM with what terrainExplained says they are, and compare aspectsSteep and the elevations with the avalanche bulletin, without turning them into a go/no-go. Where atm lists runout, avalanches from slopes above can reach the line, also below 30° and with ates 0: say so. Pass on gradeSources with the grades, and name terrain.onFoot, the part on foot above the ski depot, with the grade: it is often the steepest.

id.description: The id of a tour from winter_tours.

lang.description: Language for the grade scale and titles. Default en.

name: tour_terrain

appUrl.description: Opens this tour in the topo^alpin app, on the map. Give it to the user.

dataStale.description: True: the data is older than its source is refreshed, or the source reports a fault. Say that it may be outdated. null: unknown, not fresh.

dataUpdatedAt.description: When the data behind this answer was produced (ISO 8601, UTC; a date for a fixed release). With several sources, the oldest. null: unknown.

disclaimer.description: Automatic and possibly outdated. Pass it on.

accuracy.description: Only for estimate: how close the estimate came to grades from authors.

gradeSources.description: Each gradeSource in this answer, once: who gives the grade. Pass it on with the grades.

missing.description: Present where there is no terrain data. Pass it on.

notice.description: Terrain, not conditions. Pass it on.

source.description: The scale as published by the SAC.

scale.description: The grade on the SAC scale in the language asked for: name, steepness and the criteria of the SAC. null without a grade.

sources.description: Name these when using the data.

aspectsSteep.description: Aspects of the slopes of 30 degrees or more, on skis and on foot.

items.description: Compass direction: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW.

byClass.description: Per ATES class, share of the route.
Per ATM class, share of the route.

coverage.description: Share of the line with terrain data, 0 to 1.

footM.description: On foot above the ski depot.

aspects.description: Aspects of the slopes beside the line.

items.description: Compass direction: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW.

onFoot.description: The part on foot above the ski depot, counted apart from the part on skis; null without one. Name it with the grade: it is often the steepest.

sections.description: Stretches of the same slope class, ATES and ATM class, from start to end: elevationFromM, elevationToM, onFoot, slopeClass, steepestDeg, aspects, ates, atm, forestShare. ates is the highest ATES class within the stretch, which can be short: metres per class are in ates.byClass.

steepOnSkis.description: Metres at or above 30, 35 and 40 degrees, share of the part on skis.

steepest.description: Steepest point on skis; the part on foot is in onFoot.

terrain.description: null where there is no terrain data: unknown, not flat.

terrainExplained.description: What the terrain values mean, once per answer. Explain them when you name them.

title: Terrain of a ski or snowshoe tour
